content: Lathyrus sativus, commonly known as grass pea, is a legume belonging to the Fabaceae family. It is widely cultivated in Asia and East Africa for both human consumption and as livestock feed. This crop holds particular significance in regions prone to drought and famine, as it is considered an insurance crop due to its ability to produce reliable yields even when other crops fail. The plant is also referred to by various names, including blue sweet pea, chickling vetch, Indian pea, Indian vetch, white vetch, almorta or alverjón in Spain, cicerchia in Italy, guaya in Ethiopia, and khesari in India. In Italy, its consumption is limited to certain areas in the central part of the country and has been steadily declining. Historically, its seeds were available for human consumption in markets such as those in Florence (from organic growers) and could also be sourced through the company Manufactum several years ago. Like other grain legumes, Lathyrus sativus produces seeds that are high in protein. However, these seeds also contain varying amounts of a neurotoxic amino acid known as β-N-Oxalyl-L-α,β-diaminopropionic acid (ODAP). ODAP is recognized as the causative agent of neurolathyrism, a neurodegenerative disease that leads to paralysis of the lower body and wasting of the gluteal muscles (buttocks). Neurolathyrism has historically been observed following famines in Europe (including France, Spain, and Germany), North Africa, and South Asia. It remains prevalent in regions such as Eritrea, Ethiopia, and Afghanistan, particularly when Lathyrus seeds serve as the sole or primary source of nutrition for extended periods. Research has demonstrated that the concentration of ODAP in the plant increases when it is grown under stressful environmental conditions, exacerbating the risk of toxicity. To address this issue, breeding programs are currently underway to develop lines of Lathyrus sativus that produce lower levels of ODAP, thereby reducing the risk of neurolathyrism while maintaining the crop's resilience and nutritional value.
